purpose: Before any file exists, say who opens this, what it is called, what it must show tomorrow for it to have worked, what goes wrong and who keeps it.

questions.question: Who opens this, and what are they trying to get done?
Say it in one line someone else would understand. What should it be called?
You open it tomorrow. What do you see that tells you it worked?
Walk me through using it once, start to finish.
What is the worst wrong thing it could show, what should it show instead, and what do you do then?
Who fixes it when it breaks, and what date should it be looked at again?
Is anyone besides you going to use this?

artifact: the Product rows of APP.md, plus name and tagline in module.json; no second file

rules.rule: One line names the app in words the reader already has; it becomes name (80) and tagline (140).
Success is something you can see on open, and it is the app's done check. 'It works', 'done', 'no errors' are refused.
The failure answer names what is seen and what to do. A denial is not an answer.
The kind follows the job: a thing to look at is a page, a conversation is a chat, a shortcut to a screen is a link. The kind is chosen in the New control before the session opens.
Every app names an owner and a review date. Archiving is the end state and never deletes.
A page and a chat stay draft until the success line is true. A link is created ready because its whole surface is one server-validated screen id.
'Just me' to P7 suppresses positioning, pricing, growth and competitor questions entirely. They are never asked by default.
rules.sutra_source: FOUNDER-DIRECTIONS.md D75 ruling 4; writing-style P0 MINIMIZE
rules.enforced_by: question set; C24 and C31 promote only when P7 names someone else

rules.rule: The builder reads plain words. The thing is an app. No block names, decision ids or status lines anywhere a person reads.
One app, one job. The Founding Doctrine Simple test applied to an app; the other four tests are platform properties.

checks.what: APP.md exists at the folder root and every row id required for this kind carries a non-empty answer.
checks.evaluator: parse the APP.md tables into {row_id: answer}; assert the profile's required ids are present and non-empty; 'not recorded' (imported) is WARN not FAIL

checks.what: The P3 and P5 answers are real answers, not slogans or denials.
checks.evaluator: shared NT(cell): not in the trivial-verify blocklist, at least 5 words, P5 not matching ^(none|nothing|n/a|it can't|won't happen)

checks.what: name and tagline are present, within caps, different from each other, and the tagline is the P2 answer.
checks.evaluator: len(name) <= 80, len(tagline) <= 140, both non-empty, name != tagline case-insensitively, normalized tagline equals or is contained in the P2 cell

checks.what: No founder-only text anywhere a person reads, and the app is never called a module.
checks.evaluator: pattern scan over APP.md, name, tagline, surface.instructions and index.html text: block prefixes (INPUT:, TYPE:, ROUTE:, DEPTH:, TASK:, TRIAGE:, OS:), +-- FLOW/BLUEPRINT/DISPATCH, ATOM:, BUILD-LAYER, ROUTING PIN, dref-, ADR-nnn, D-Mnn/Dnn, and 'module' outside module.json, /api/modules, ~/.sutra-ui/modules
WARN when P1 contains ' and also ', ' as well as ', ';' or more than two sentences
